doc.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: The Playboy Club job with Cal Collins and deciding to leave Cincinnati
summary: He played a trio job with Cal Collins at the Cincinnati Playboy Club, then chose to move to New York rather than repeat his father's dead end.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Was there a conscious decision at some point, you said I have to move to New York?

Yeah, there was. I was I think 24. I’d come back after working with Woody and I went back and starting working — I had a great job in Cincinnati in the Playboy Club, actually with Cal Collins, who’s on this, and I’ve known Cal since I was a kid. He actually was a friend of my father’s. And Cal is one of the great jazz guitar players. I don’t know if you’re familiar with his playing, but he’s always been great, and we had a steady job at the Playboy Club for a couple of years — two and a half years, something like that. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

As a trio, with Ron McCurdy, a drummer who lived there. And it was the best job, to this day, that I’ve ever had. And it was playing jazz five hours a night with a great group and bunnies to look at and great food. And I thought the music business is wonderful. And I didn’t know it was going to be steadily downhill from there. And then that came to an end, that job came to an end and I thought well I mean it’s back to the same cycle of clubs and stuff in Cincinnati. And I figured well it’s time to move to New York. My father never left town, he always stayed in Cincinnati. And I profited I think by his example that, to a degree it was a dead end street for him. He was a much better player and would have had a much better career I think had he moved or taken — he had chances to leave and he didn’t. So I thought I didn’t want to make that mistake.
